components.title: Project starting-point chooser
components.purpose: Help a visitor choose a starting conversation, then show the relevant preparation and next step.
components.notes: Load components/choice-script.html once per page. Unique id per instance. Native radios support keyboard selection; all option panels remain readable without JavaScript. This is guidance, not a diagnosis or quotation.

example.title: What brings your opening in today?
example.intro: Pick the nearest description. Jeff would prefer to meet the door, but Doreen says we can start here.

options.label: I want a new door
options.title: Start with the room, not the shopping cart.
options.body: Gather a photo of the opening and the look you have in mind. Discuss space, privacy, and the selected product before ordering. Jeff has already imagined the first Christmas.

options.label: My existing door needs attention
options.summary: There has been a change in the relationship.
options.title: Describe what changed.
options.body: Note the movement or noise you have noticed and gather any model details. This chooser cannot establish the cause. Jeff is trying very hard not to ask whether the door has been distant.

options.label: I’m still figuring it out
options.title: Bring the question you actually have.
options.body: A photo and a short description are enough to begin a conversation. You do not need the right vocabulary. Jeff once referred to a room as “the area around the door.”

example.note: Parody framing around general preparation prompts. Choosing an option sends nothing, books nothing, and saves nothing.
